skill.name: hig-inputs
skill.description: Apply Apple Human Interface Guidelines for input methods across Apple platforms, including gestures, keyboards, Apple Pencil, remotes, controllers, motion sensors, eye tracking, and spatial interactions.
skill.summary: Design input experiences that follow Apple HIG guidance across Apple platforms.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The scanned files are a documentation-only Apple HIG input guide with bundled markdown references. All static findings are false positives caused by design terms, markdown screenshots, inline-code path formatting, and plain markdown links. No prompt injection, code execution, data exfiltration, or active network behavior was found.

content.value_statement: Designing inputs across Apple platforms is easy to miss when touch, keyboard, pointer, Pencil, controllers, and spatial devices overlap. This skill gives Claude, Codex, and Claude Code focused HIG guidance for practical input recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Summarizes Apple HIG input principles for touch, keyboard, pointer, Apple Pencil, remotes, and game controllers.
Maps platform-specific input expectations for iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS.
Suggests gesture behavior, focus movement, shortcut conventions, and accessibility alternatives.
Uses bundled reference files for Apple Pencil, Camera Control, Digital Crown, and spatial input topics.
Prompts for missing platform and device details only after checking project context.
limitations: It does not run tests or inspect live application behavior.
It uses bundled guidance and may lag behind the latest Apple documentation.
It cannot replace accessibility testing with real devices and assistive technologies.
It does not generate production code unless the user separately asks for implementation.

use_cases.title: Plan Cross-Platform Inputs
use_cases.description: Define input methods for an Apple app that spans touch, keyboard, pointer, and spatial devices.

use_cases.title: Review Gesture Behavior
use_cases.description: Check whether custom gestures conflict with Apple system gestures or need clearer feedback.

use_cases.title: Map Controller Fallbacks
use_cases.description: Plan game controller, keyboard, and touch alternatives for games on Apple platforms.

prompt_templates.title: Get Input Guidance
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my app idea for Apple input methods. Platform: [platform]. Main tasks: [tasks]. Recommend suitable inputs and accessibility alternatives.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Platform Patterns
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare input expectations for [feature] on iPadOS, macOS, and visionOS. Include touch, pointer, keyboard, and focus guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Interaction Spec
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this interaction spec against Apple HIG input guidance: [paste spec]. Flag conflicts, missing fallbacks, and unclear feedback.

prompt_templates.title: Design Multi-Device Control Model
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a control model for [product] across [platforms]. Include gestures, keyboard shortcuts, focus rules, controller mapping, and accessibility alternatives.

output_examples.input: A drawing app for iPad with Pencil, touch, and keyboard support.
output: Prioritize immediate Pencil ink response and use touch for panning or selection.
Support Scribble in text fields and expose common keyboard shortcuts.
Add clear undo paths for double-tap, squeeze, and custom tool actions.

output_examples.input: A tvOS video app with a remote, focusable cards, and an electronic program guide.
output: Make every interactive element reachable through focus navigation.
Differentiate tap and press actions so accidental input does not activate content.
Support expected EPG browsing buttons when compatible remotes provide them.

output_examples.input: A visionOS collaboration app that uses gaze, pinch, and direct hand interaction.
output: Use generous targets because eye tracking is less precise than touch.
Avoid sustained gaze for activation and provide clear hover feedback.
Offer accessible alternatives for gestures that require specific body positions.

best_practices: Name target Apple platforms before asking for detailed input advice.
Provide existing interaction specs, wireframes, or accessibility goals when available.
Ask for alternatives when one input method is unavailable or fatiguing.
anti_patterns: Assume touch-only behavior works across every Apple platform.
Use custom gestures without clear feedback, fallback controls, and accessibility support.
Treat bundled guidance as proof that a shipped UI meets current Apple review expectations.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps design Apple app input behavior using bundled Human Interface Guidelines references.

faq.question: Which platforms does it cover?
faq.answer: It covers iOS, iPadOS, macOS, watchOS, tvOS, and visionOS input patterns.

faq.question: Can it review custom gestures?
faq.answer: Yes. It can flag gesture conflicts and recommend feedback, discoverability, and fallback options.

faq.question: Does it replace accessibility testing?
faq.answer: No. Use it for planning, then test with real devices and assistive technologies.

faq.question: Does it need project context?
faq.answer: It first checks existing Apple design context when available, then asks only for missing details.

faq.question: Can Claude Code or Codex use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
